title: Persistent Cognitive Architectures for Human-AI Co-Reasoning: Beyond Retrieval to Structural Intelligence
description: Introduces Symbiose, a persistent cognitive architecture that integrates knowledge graphs, vector search, causal tracking, hierarchical memory consolidation, and proactive triggers via the Quantum Leap (QL) orchestration layer. The system provides epistemic honesty through an L0–L3 tagging framework and demonstrates emergent, persistent co-reasoning capabilities in a longitudinal Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) use case beyond stateless RAG baselines.
author: Morten Magnusson

fused_relevance_score.description: Hybrid ranking that combines embedding similarity with graph-structural relevance in Graph–Vector Fusion.

structural_score.description: Structural contribution to the fused score, rewarding shorter graph paths connecting the query to a retrieved result.

key_results.main_finding: Symbiose demonstrates persistent, proactive, and provenance-tagged co-reasoning—enabling cross-session identity linking, hierarchical memory consolidation, proactive suggestions, and explicit L0–L3 epistemic tagging beyond stateless RAG.
datasets_used: Longitudinal interaction logs from a year-long Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) theory-development deployment
Project knowledge graph (Neo4j) and vector store (Qdrant) content used during the deployment

kill_criteria: KC1: If a stateless RAG baseline reproduces the same set of emergent behaviors (cross-session identity linking, proactive suggestions, and explicit provenance) under identical tasks without external persistent structure, the claim that persistence is required is falsified.
KC2: If any system responses in evaluation lack L0–L3 epistemic tags, the claim that every response is epistemically tagged is falsified.
KC3: If L0/L1/L2 claims cannot be traced to verifiable sources or derivations upon audit, the epistemic honesty/provenance claim is falsified.

KC4: If Graph–Vector Fusion does not outperform pure vector retrieval on multi-hop or causal-retrieval tasks (e.g., discovers no additional correct connections), the structural-intelligence claim is falsified.
KC5: If proactive triggers fail to produce any user-accepted suggestions during sustained operation on comparable tasks, the proactive autonomy claim is falsified.
KC6: If hierarchical memory consolidation yields no cross-session reuse of consolidated memories during longitudinal operation, the temporal cognition claim is falsified.
abstract: While retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enables large language models to access external knowledge, it remains fundamentally reactive and stateless. We present Symbiose, a cognitive architecture that combines graph-based causal reasoning, temporal pattern recognition, and proactive autonomy to enable persistent, evolving collaboration between humans and AI. Components are integrated through Quantum Leap (QL), a persistent cognitive orchestration layer. Every response is tagged via an L0–L3 epistemic framework distinguishing canonical facts from LLM-generated hypotheses.
